lesson_title: Shoes Before Socks: Undo Buttons in Reverse Order
hook_text: 3x minus 5 equals 16. Which do you undo first, the times 3 or the minus 5? Get it backwards and you are swimming in fractions.
clip_script: An equation is a list of things done to x. 3x minus 5 equals 16: x was multiplied by 3, then 5 was taken off. To get x back, press the undo buttons in reverse order, like taking off shoes before socks. The last thing done was take off 5, so undo it first: add 5 to both sides. 3x equals 21. The first thing done was times 3, so undo it last: divide both sides by 3. x equals 7. Check: 3 times 7 is 21, take off 5 is 16. Both sides, every time, because an equation is a scale that must stay balanced. Watch the trap: 10 minus 2x equals 4. Take 10 off: negative 2x equals negative 6. Divide by NEGATIVE 2: x is 3. Divide by plain 2 and you get negative 3, and the check fails. Reverse order, both sides, check.
visual_style: A balance scale on a whiteboard with an x-box on one side; undo buttons light up in reverse order as each line is written beneath; a wrong division flashes red and the check ticks green.
pacing: A clear rule, one worked anchor at speaking pace, one trap, one check.
